output.summary: A coniferous tree native to eastern North America. It can live for more than 500 years and tolerates deep shade, moist soil and slopes. Much of its range is threatened by the invasive hemlock woolly adelgid, which can eventually kill the trees.
output.edibilityNote: Tea has historically been made from leafy twigs or needles; the inner bark can be eaten raw or boiled and made into flour.
